name: Thirteen Colonies to Fifty States: Making the USA
description: Settlers, a revolution, a constitution and a century of expansion: how a string of colonies grew into a continental country.

checkpoints.name: Claims and settlements
checkpoints.note: Spain, France and England each stake claims in North America. English settlers found Virginia in 1607 and the Pilgrims and Puritans found Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay.

checkpoints.name: Revolution
checkpoints.note: Britain wins North America from France in 1763 but then taxes its colonies. The colonists declare independence in 1776, and the Treaty of Paris in 1783 recognises their new country.

checkpoints.name: A new republic
checkpoints.note: The Constitution sets up the federal government, and the Louisiana Purchase doubles the land. Texas breaks from Mexico, joins the Union, and a war with Mexico adds California and the Southwest.

checkpoints.name: Union and empire
checkpoints.note: The Gold Rush fills California and the Civil War tests the Union against the Confederacy. By the end of the century the United States holds Alaska and has taken over Hawaii, Cuba and the Philippines.

checkpoints.name: The last states
checkpoints.note: The country takes its present shape when Alaska and Hawaii become the forty-ninth and fiftieth states in 1959. Cuba and the Philippines become independent along the way.
